events.title: Retail sales (Oct)
events.note: Scheduled one hour before the U.S. stock market opens.

brief.context: Retail sales rose 0.8% in September after a revised 1.3% gain in August, with gas station receipts lifted by higher fuel prices. Inflation has stayed above 3% and markets are pricing a Fed rate increase in December, so policymakers are watching whether consumer spending is holding up. This is the main read on October spending before the Fed's December 8-9 meeting.

events.recap: Retail sales came in at 0.2% against a 0.2% forecast, in line with expectations. The previous reading was 0.8%.

events.title: Initial jobless claims
events.note: Weekly initial claims for unemployment insurance.
facts: The initial claims reading was the highest since week to Sep 5.
events.recap: Jobless claims came in at 203K against a 198K forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 200K, revised to 202K. 4-week average 198K (previous 196K); Continuing claims 1.76M (previous 1.69M). The initial claims reading was the highest since week to Sep 5.

facts: It was the fifth monthly increase in a row.

events.title: GDP, second estimate (Q3)
events.note: Scheduled one hour before the U.S. stock market opens.

brief.context: The advance estimate showed the economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, above the 3.2% economists had expected, led by consumer spending. This second estimate revises that figure with more complete data. It lands the same morning as the October PCE inflation report, two weeks before the Fed's December meeting.

facts: The real GDP, annualized reading was the highest since Q3 2023.
events.recap: GDP came in at 4.3% against a 3.5% forecast, above expectations. The previous reading was 3.4%. The real GDP, annualized reading was the highest since Q3 2023.

events.note: Weekly initial claims for unemployment insurance.

events.recap: Jobless claims came in at 189K against a 201K forecast, below expectations. The previous reading was 203K, revised to 202K. 4-week average 196K (previous 198K); Continuing claims 1.70M (previous 1.79M). The initial claims reading was the lowest since week to Jul 18.

events.title: PCE inflation · Personal income and outlays (Oct)
events.note: Scheduled one hour before the U.S. stock market opens.

brief.context: Core PCE prices rose 0.3% in September and 3.1% from a year earlier, up from 3.0% in August, while the headline index was up 3.6% on the year. PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, and markets are pricing a rate increase at the December 8-9 meeting. October CPI, released November 10, showed core consumer prices up 0.3% for a third straight month.

events.recap: Core PCE came in at 0.3% against a 0.3% forecast, in line with expectations. The previous reading was 0.3%. PCE m/m 0.3% (previous 0.5%); Core PCE y/y 3.3% (previous 3.1%); Personal spending m/m 0.3% (previous 0.6%).
